## Python

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from dgxe import *

wx = pd.read_csv("data/narrabri_weather.csv")
traj = pd.read_csv("data/narrabri_biomass.csv.gz")
drv = make_drivers(wx)
Theta = make_library(drv)
tr = make_trajectories(traj, drv)
```

:::


Every method maps the design matrix $\mathbf{X}$ and the increments $\Delta\mathbf{y}$ of one genotype to a coefficient vector, with the intercept first. A method is therefore a function `fit(X, dy)`, and methods can be exchanged freely. Genotype `g001` is used here.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## Least squares and penalised regression

Ordinary least squares uses `lm.fit` (Python: `numpy.linalg.lstsq`). Ridge, lasso and elastic net are provided by `glmnet` (Python: scikit-learn `ElasticNet` for lasso and elastic net and a closed form for ridge, with the penalty scaled as in `glmnet`); they differ in the penalty (squared, absolute value, and a mixture of both). The lasso sets coefficients to zero.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_ols", "fit_glmnet", "fit_ridge", "fit_lasso", "fit_enet")
```

## Subset selection and thresholding

Best-subset selection and backward elimination keep $k$ terms (`leaps`; in Python the residual sums of squares are computed directly from the Gram matrix). Sequential thresholded least squares (STLSQ) is the algorithm of the original SINDy method: fit, remove the terms whose scaled coefficient is below a threshold, and refit on the remaining terms.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("fit_subset", "fit_stlsq")
```

Scaled to a common size (coefficient times the standard deviation of the term, relative to that of the increments), the sparsity pattern of each method is visible; empty cells are terms that were removed.

## Python

```python
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap, TwoSlopeNorm

size = d.X.std(axis=0, ddof=1) / d.dy.std(ddof=1)
effect = fits.iloc[1:].mul(size, axis=0)
colours = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("dgxe", [BURGUNDY, "white", BLUE])
colours.set_bad("#F3F4F6")                       # removed terms

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.6))
image = ax.imshow(effect.where(effect != 0), cmap=colours,
                  norm=TwoSlopeNorm(0), aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(effect.shape[1]), effect.columns, rotation=30, ha="right")
ax.set_yticks(range(effect.shape[0]), effect.index)
fig.colorbar(image, label="scaled coefficient")
fig.tight_layout()
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: 04-3-run
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 3.6
size <- apply(d$X, 2, sd) / sd(d$dy)
effect <- fits[-1, ] * size
long <- data.frame(term = factor(rownames(effect), rev(rownames(effect))),
                   method = factor(rep(colnames(effect), each = nrow(effect)),
                                   colnames(effect)),
                   effect = as.vector(effect))

ggplot(long, aes(method, term, fill = ifelse(effect == 0, NA, effect))) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = dgxe[["burgundy"]], mid = "white",
                       high = dgxe[["blue"]], na.value = "#F3F4F6") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "scaled\ncoefficient") +
  theme_dgxe() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right")
```

The coefficients of correlated terms are not determined individually (powers of one driver, and thermal time and day length, are strongly correlated), so the selected terms differ between methods. The methods are compared by prediction on unseen seasons in step 5.

## Exploring a method

Each method has one hyperparameter: the threshold of STLSQ, the penalty $\lambda$ of ridge, lasso and elastic net, or the number of terms $k$ of subset selection. The left panel shows the scaled coefficients of `g001` for the chosen setting, and the right panel the held-out trajectory error (20 genotypes) for all settings of the method.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
d3 = window.d3          // local copies, see js/
Plot = window.Plot
hyper = FileAttachment("data/interactive/hyper.json").json()
viewof method = select("Method", Object.keys(hyper.methods), "STLSQ")
spec = hyper.methods[method]
viewof step = slider(spec.param, spec.values, Math.floor(spec.values.length / 2), v => (+v).toPrecision(2))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const all = Object.values(hyper.methods);
  const reach = d3.max(all.flatMap(m => m.effect.flat().map(Math.abs)));
  const rmse = [d3.min(all.flatMap(m => m.rmse)), 0.8];   // cap: very large penalties are off scale
  const rows = hyper.terms.map((term, i) => ({term, effect: spec.effect[step][i]}));
  const curve = spec.values.map((value, i) => ({value, rmse: spec.rmse[i]}));
  const scale = spec.param === "terms" ? "linear" : "log";
  const coefficients = Plot.plot({
    width: 340, height: 300, marginLeft: 50,
    x: {domain: [-reach, reach], label: "scaled coefficient"},
    y: {domain: hyper.terms, label: null},
    marks: [Plot.barX(rows, {x: "effect", y: "term",
              fill: d => d.effect > 0 ? "#014E81" : "#8B1E3F"}),
            Plot.ruleX([0])]
  });
  const error = Plot.plot({
    width: 340, height: 300,
    x: {type: scale, label: spec.param, tickFormat: ".2~g"},
    y: {domain: [rmse[0] - 0.01, rmse[1] + 0.01], label: "held-out RMSE (t/ha)"},
    marks: [Plot.line(curve, {x: "value", y: "rmse", stroke: "#9CA3AF", clip: true}),
            Plot.dot(curve, {x: "value", y: "rmse", fill: "#9CA3AF", r: 3, clip: true}),
            Plot.dot([curve[step]], {x: "value", y: "rmse", fill: "#8B1E3F", r: 6, clip: true})]
  });
  return html`<div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:1rem">${coefficients}${error}</div>
    <p class="interactive-note">${spec.nterms[step]} of ${hyper.terms.length} terms retained.</p>`;
}
```

The figure uses results computed beforehand ([`scripts/precompute_interactive.R`](https://github.com/corne00/dynamic-gxe-workshop/blob/main/scripts/precompute_interactive.R)).
